{{short description|German biophysicist}}
'''Ilme Schlichting''' (born March 8, 1960) is a German [[biophysics|biophysicist]].

== Academic work ==

Ilme Schlichting studied biology and physics at the [[University of Heidelberg]] from 1979 to 1987. She earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in biology there in 1990. Schlichting pursued post-doctoral studies at the [[Max Planck Institute for Medical Research]] and at [[Brandeis University]] in [[Boston]] in the United States as a Feodor Lynen Fellow. From 1994 to 2001 she was head of a working group at the [[Max Planck Institute of Molecular Physiology]] in [[Dortmund]]. Since 2002 she is director of the department for Biomolecular Mechanisms at the [[Max Planck Institute for Medical Research]].

Schlichting has studied the structure and operation of [[biomolecule]]s using [[protein crystallization|protein crystallography]]. During her PhD she made important contributions to the understanding of the switch function of the [[Michaelis–Menten kinetics|Michaelis complex]] and hence to the understanding of this [[enzyme]] during her doctorate using the Laue method.<ref name=dfg>{{cite web |url=https://www.dfg.de/en/service/press/press_releases/1999/press_release_no_54/index.html |title=Prizes in the Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Programme 2000 |date=December 3, 1999 |publisher=Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
Recently, Schlichting has been one of the founders of time-resolved [[X-ray crystallography| protein crystallography]] at [[Free-electron laser]]s.

*Karl Lohmann Prize, 1991
*[[Otto Hahn Medal]], 1991
*[[Ernst Schering Prize]], 1998<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scheringstiftung.de/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=38&Itemid=28&lang=en |title=Ernst Schering Prize |publisher=Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft |access-date=2015-11-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223181839/http://www.scheringstiftung.de/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=38&Itemid=28&lang=en |archive-date=2017-12-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref> 
*[[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]], [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]], 2000<ref name=dfg/>
*Member of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]], 2003
*Carus Medal, 2003
*Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], 2003
*Cross of Merit of [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]], 2008
*Spiers Memorial Award of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], 2018
